svg.text: #597 Enterprise Structured Output: XGrammar / llguidance Zero-Overhead Bitmask & Jump-Forward
Cloud & AI Solution Architect Guide · 100.0% Valid JSON Schema · 0.05ms Bitmask + 26.5% Jump-Forward Speedup vs. +28% Retry Waste
1. Three Generations of Structured JSON Decoding
Gen 1: Prompt-Only + 3x Pydantic Validation Retry Loop
• 11.4% schema failure rate on 40-field ERP JSON → P99 latency explodes 3.2x (4.48s)
• Wastes +28% GPU Decode tokens re-generating failed JSON payloads
Gen 2: Naive Uncached Regex FSM (Legacy Outlines / Guidance v0.1)
• Scans 128,000-vocab token table on CPU every step (18ms–32ms CPU stall/token!)
• Doubles TPOT from 12.0ms to 34.0ms and takes 12s to compile large schemas
Gen 3: XGrammar / llguidance Pushdown Automaton + Jump-Forward
• Pre-separates Context-Independent vs. Dependent tokens: 0.05ms CPU mask/step!
• Jump-Forward Fast-Forwards deterministic JSON keys ("order_id": "), cutting
autoregressive Decode steps by 26.5% (Faster than unconstrained free-text!)
2. Jump-Forward Mechanics & 100-QPS Fleet ROI
Why Constrained JSON Is 26.5% FASTER Than Free-Text Generation
• In a 320-token ERP JSON object, 85 tokens (26.5%) are deterministic schema keys,
quotes, colons, and braces (e.g., {"transaction_status": "APPROVED", "items": [)
• SGLang / vLLM V1 Jump-Forward appends those 85 tokens in ONE prefill step
• Reduces expensive HBM-bound Decode steps from 320 to 235 (-26.5% E2EL!)
100 QPS Structured Extraction Fleet Sizing (70B-FP8 on H200)
• Prompt-Only + Retry Loop: 11.4% retries + 320 decode steps → 12× H200 ($40.8k/mo)
• Legacy Uncached FSM: 34ms TPOT bottleneck → 20× H200 ($68.0k/mo)
• XGrammar / llguidance + Jump-Forward: 0% retries + 235 steps → 8× H200 ($27.2k/mo)
• Saves $13,600/mo (-33.3%) vs. Prompt-Retry while achieving 100.00% schema validity!
3. Schema Ordering Pitfall: Always Place "reasoning_summary" BEFORE "decision_enum" in JSON!
• Autoregressive LLMs condition each field on preceding tokens. Putting {"verdict": "REJECT", "reason": "..."} forces a blind guess first!
• Ordering fields as {"step_by_step_analysis": "...", "verdict": "REJECT"} lifts classification accuracy from 79.4% to 95.8% (+16.4 pts).
